etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From bake +‎ -ery (“place of”). Replaced earlier bakehouse. Originally “place for making bread”; as “shop where baked goods are sold”, it was noted as an Americanism by British travelers by 1832.

This etymology is incomplete. You can help Wiktionary by elaborating on the origins of this term.

definitions.definition: A place in which bread (and often other baked goods such as cakes) is baked and/or sold.

quote.citation: 1970-1975, Lou Sullivan, personal diary, quoted in 2019, Ellis Martin, Zach Ozma (editors), We Both Laughed In Pleasure
quote.text: Bridget & Jacob were coming home from the hospital bout 11:30. Kathy & I made a little "brunch" of bakery & coffee.

quote.text: Then, later, I think I saw them at Lemke's Tomahawk Foods getting roasted chicken from the delicatessen and at Nelson's County Market picking up some bakery and fruit. It looked like they were going on a picnic.

quote.citation: 2011 September 7, Ann Carol, Dark Places‎[2], Author House, →ISBN, page 196:
quote.text: She set about preparing the house for everyone to come over. She and Danielle made the sandwiches and put them in the refrigerator. They got out plates, glasses, napkins and silverware and set up a buffet table. Chuck went to the bakery and got some bakery.

quote.citation: 2017 May 1, James S. Peters, Sadakichi Hartmann, Alien Son: A Biography‎[3], Sunstone Press, →ISBN, →LCCN, →OCLC, page 121:
quote.text: Perhaps she would be able to bring me something to eat in the evening. Still it was doubtful if she could get away. I better had let her buy some bakery for me. With some inconceivable pride, or rather stubbornness, as I wanted money, I refused. In consequence, I suffered all night and the next day and the following night.

quote.citation: 2018 December 15, Hannah Katherine Klumb, The Suicide Bridge‎[4], Waterton Publishing Company, →ISBN, page 35:
quote.text: “The next morning I woke up and she was fast asleep. Guess I did pass out for a while. So I thought I would go surprise her, and I bought her some flowers and picked up some bakery in town. But when I got back, she wasn't in bed.  […] ”
